title: Effectiveness of video-based counselling according to Marte Meo for improving the quality of child-directed speech of parents with their cochlear implant-fitted children.
summary:
In Germany, it is standard practice for children with cochlear implants (CI) to receive family-centered, hearing-focused intervention as part of CI follow-up therapy (AWMF S2k 017-071). However, there is currently little evidence for hearing-focused approaches in the therapy of children with hearing impairments (Neumann, K et al. 2022). The planned study therefore aims to statistically examine the effectiveness of video-supported counseling based on Marte Meo for the language-promoting interaction behavior of parents with their CI-equipped children within the framework of CI follow-up therapy. 
In addition, another goal is to increase the chances of CI-equipped children for optimal hearing and language development, and thus for social participation. If a higher number of intervention sessions is shown to have a demonstrably beneficial effect on child development, this should in the future be standardly incorporated into the concept of CI follow-up therapy. Based on various criteria (educational level, multilingualism, child's age, additional disabilities), the participants are assigned to the intervention or information group as evenly as possible. Changes between the first and second measurements are assessed in the aspects that were the focus of the counseling using an observation form (EKIE-hör; evaluated by several raters with calculation of the mean) as well as a computer program for assessing interaction (Interact). In addition, the deltas between the first and second measurements are tested for significance and effect between the intervention and information groups.
conditions: Presence of otological and audiological implants

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Families with a child who has a cochlear implant
Sufficient knowledge of German
Currently undergoing follow-up therapy for cochlear implants at CIC Friedberg
Written consent to participate in the study
Normal nonverbal cognitive development (SON-R) at the start of the study ≥90
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient knowledge of German.
